name: Banana Leaf Rice
hint: South Indian rice on banana leaf with vegetable sides, rasam, curries, papadom and refillable rice; calories vary hugely with how many curry and rice refills you take; flag the refill trap

name: Varuval
hint: South Indian/mamak dry-fried spiced meat with a thick clinging masala, less gravy than curry but more oil; variants chicken varuval, mutton varuval

name: Kari Ayam (Chicken Curry)
hint: chicken curry in spiced gravy; variants mamak (thinner, oilier), kampung (coconut-based), with potato; the gravy oil and santan drive calories, the chicken is lean

name: Kari Kambing (Mutton Curry)
hint: mutton/goat curry in rich spiced gravy; fattier than chicken curry because of the mutton fat and oil; mamak staple with bread or rice

name: Tandoori Chicken
hint: yogurt and spice marinated chicken roasted in a tandoor; relatively lean if you skip the skin, one of the better mamak protein choices; usually eaten with naan

name: Naan
hint: tandoor-baked leavened flatbread; variants plain, butter, garlic, cheese; butter and cheese versions add a lot, plain is just refined flour carbs

name: Chapati
hint: wholemeal unleavened flatbread, lighter and higher fibre than naan, little to no oil; eaten with dhal or curry; a smarter mamak bread choice

name: Roti Tisu
hint: giant paper-thin crispy cone-shaped sweet roti dusted with sugar and often condensed milk; mostly sugar and ghee, a dessert disguised as bread

name: Poori (Puri)
hint: small deep-fried puffed wheat bread served with potato curry (aloo) and dhal; oil absorbed in deep frying drives calories

name: Samosa
hint: deep-fried pastry triangle with spiced filling; variants vegetable (potato/peas), chicken; pastry and frying oil are most of the calories

name: Pakora
hint: chickpea-batter fritters deep fried; variants vegetable pakora, onion bhaji; batter plus absorbed oil drive calories

name: Lassi
hint: blended yogurt drink; variants sweet mango lassi (sugar and fruit puree), salted lassi (much lower calorie); sugar is the main calorie driver in sweet versions

name: Teh Halia
hint: pulled ginger milk tea with condensed and evaporated milk; similar to teh tarik plus ginger; condensed milk sugar and fat drive calories

name: Chicken 65
hint: South Indian/mamak spicy deep-fried battered chicken bites, bright red, tossed in curry leaf and chili; batter and deep frying make it calorie dense

name: Lempeng
hint: Malay coconut pancake/crepe cooked on a griddle; variants kelapa (coconut), pisang (banana), jagung (corn); eaten with sambal or sugar; modest unless lots of oil

name: Kuih Putu
hint: steamed rice-flour kuih with gula melaka centre and grated coconut; variants putu bambu (steamed in bamboo tubes), putu piring (disc shaped); palm sugar drives calories

name: Kuih Bom
hint: deep-fried dough ball with sweet grated coconut or chocolate filling, sometimes sesame coated; dough plus filling plus frying oil

name: Kuih Siput
hint: crunchy fried snail-shaped savoury snack made from spiced dough, a popular Raya cookie eaten by the handful; flour and frying oil, easy to overeat

name: Kuih Ros (Kuih Loyang)
hint: deep-fried crispy rose/honeycomb cookie made by dipping a brass mould in coconut-egg batter then frying; light per piece but oily, eaten many at a time

name: Tepung Pelita
hint: two-layer pandan and salted coconut-milk kuih steamed in small banana-leaf cups, a Ramadan bazaar staple; santan and sugar drive calories

name: Amplang
hint: bite-sized fish crackers from Sabah/Sarawak/East Coast made from mackerel and sago flour, deep fried and puffy; variants ikan, udang; oil and easy snacking volume

name: Kuih Kapit (Love Letters)
hint: thin crisp folded wafer of egg, coconut milk and sugar pressed in a hot mould, a Chinese New Year staple; variants kuih sepit/sapit; light each but eaten in quantity

name: Keropok Keping
hint: flat fish crackers (sliced and sun-dried then deep fried), the keping form of keropok; per piece light but absorbs oil and eaten with sweet chili dip
